topics.title: About TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

items.q: What is "TDS and TCS Credit Received" Statement?

spans.s: “TDS and TCS Credit Received” Statement has been provided at Returns Dashboard, to all the Deductees and suppliers, from whom some amount of tax has been deducted or collected at source, by the persons registered as Tax Deductors/ e-commerce operators, respectively. This TDS and TCS Received Statement will be used to take action on auto populated details of Tax Deducted or Collected at Source, as indicated in the return filed in Form GSTR-7/ 8 of said Tax Deductor/ e-commerce operator for a tax period.

items.q: TDS and TCS Credit Received comprises of which tables?

spans.s:
TDS/ TCS Credit Received Statement comprises of below tables basis details filed by Tax Deductors/ e-commerce operator in Form GSTR-7/8 for taking action therein:
 1. TDS Credit Received: To accept/ reject TDS Credit Received details
 2. Amendments of TDS Credit Received: To accept/ reject amendments to TDS Credit Received details
 3. TCS Credit Received: To accept/ reject TCS Credit Received details
 4. Amendments of TCS Credit Received: To accept/ reject amendments to TCS Credit Received details
 Filing TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

items.q: Who needs to file TDS and TCS Credit Received?
items.section: Filing TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s: TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement has to be filed by the taxpayers whose tax is deducted or collected by the Deductor/ e-commerce operator, respectively.

items.q: Is it mandatory to file TDS and TCS Credit Received statement for every tax period?
items.section: Filing TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s: Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received statement for every tax period is not mandatory. It is required to be filed when any amount is deducted or collected by the recipient.

items.q: From where can I as a taxpayer file TDS and TCS Credit Received?
items.section: Filing TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s:
TDS and TCS Credit Received can be accessed on the GST Portal, post login in the Returns Dashboard by the taxpayer.
 The path is
Services > Returns > TDS and TCS credit received

.
 Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

items.q: What options are available in Action field?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: The following two options are available in Action field.

items.q: What will happen if I reject the TDS/ TCS Credit Received amount?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: Rejected records will flow to Form GSTR-7/8 of the respective Deductor/ e-commerce operator for amendments, as the case may be, after filing of “TDS/ TCS Credit Received” statement by the Deductee/ supplier, from whom tax is deducted or collected at source. Deductor/ e-commerce operator will make amendments on those records.

items.q: What will happen if I accept the TDS/ TCS Credit Received amount?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: Accepted TDS/ TCS credit amount will be credited to your Electronic Cash Ledger only after filing of “TDS/ TCS Credit Received” statement. You can use that cash for payment of any tax liability or take refund.

items.q: Can I change the accepted records?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: Accepted records which have been filed in TDS/ TCS Credit Received statement cannot be changed.

items.q: What will happen if Deductee/ supplier files the TDS/TDS Credit received statement without taking any action on the TDS/TCS details auto populated from filed GSTR-7/8?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: Deductee/ supplier cannot file TDS/ TCS Credit received statement without taking any action on the TDS/TCS details auto populated from filed GSTR-7/8.

items.q: When all Summary tiles of TDS/TCS credit received and Amendment to TDS/TCS credit received will be updated?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: All tile summaries will be updated after taking accept/ reject action on auto-populated records inside each tile.

items.q: When Rejected TDS or TCS record will flow to GSTR-7/ 8 of Deductor/E-com operator?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: After successful filing of TDS and TCS credit Received statement by the Deductee/ supplier, rejected records will flow to Form GSTR-7 of Tax Deductor or to Form GSTR-8 of E-com operator of the subsequent tax period. These records will be available in Table 4 – Rejected tabs of respective returns for amendment by Deductor/ e-commerce Operator.

items.q: Can I file TDS and TCS Credit Received statement without taking action on all auto populated records?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: No. You can’t file the TDS and TCS Credit received statement without taking action on all auto populated records in all tables.

items.q: TDS or TCS record has been amended by Deductor or E-com operator (Collector) in Form GSTR-7/8. Where can I see such amended record in TDS and TCS Credit received statement?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: All amended records will be available in amendment tables of TDS and TCS Credit received statement.

items.q: Can I revert (undo) the Action (Accept to Reject or Reject or Accept)?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: Yes, you can change the action till you file the TDS and TCS credit Received statement. You cannot change the action after filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received statement.

items.q: Can I (from whom the tax is collected or deducted at source), edit the TDS or TCS records, auto populated in my TDS and TCS Credit Received statement?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: No. You can’t edit the auto populated records. If auto populated records are not correct, then you can only reject the record.

items.q: Can I add any new record in any table in TDS and TCS Credit Received statement?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: No. You can’t add new record in any table in TDS and TCS Credit Received statement.

items.q: Can I take any action, if the deductor / e-commerce operator has amended any record before taking action by me?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: If the deductor / e-commerce operator has amended any record before taking action by you, the same will be disabled for taking any action. You need to take action of accept/reject on latest amended record auto-populated in the subsequent tax period.

items.q: Can a deductee file TDS and TCS Credit Received for a future period without taking action in the previous period?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: Yes, the GST system allows a deductee to file TDS and TCS Credit Received for any future period even if no action was taken or the form was not filed for a previous period. This is because TDS and TCS Credit Received is not a sequential form. Deductee can claim TDS/TCS credits for any available period without being restricted by earlier filings.

items.q: Can a deductee file TDS and TCS Credit Received for a future period after taking action in the previous period but not filing it?
items.section: Taking Action on TDS and TCS Credit Received Amount

spans.s: No, if a deductee takes action (accepts or rejects invoices) in the TDS & TCS Credit Received form for a previous month (e.g., M1) but does not file it, the GST system will not allow filing of TDS & TCS Credit Received for the next month (e.g., M2). An error message will be displayed, and the future period’s filing will be blocked until the previous period’s TDS and TCS Credit Received is filed.

items.q: By when do I need to file TDS and TCS Credit Received statement and is there any late fee for late filing?

spans.s: There is no due date or late fee for filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received. Cash ledger will be credited by the amount equal to the Tax Deducted/Collected, only after filing of the statement.

items.q: Can I file TDS and TCS Credit Received statement multiple times during a month?

spans.s: You can file TDS and TCS Credit Received statement only once for a tax period. This statement is tax period specific.

items.q: Can I file TDS and TCS Credit Received statement through offline mode?

spans.s: Yes, TDS and TCS Credit Received statement can be filed only through offline mode.

items.q: Can I preview TDS and TCS Credit Received statement before filing?

spans.s: Yes, you can view/download the preview of TDS and TCS Credit Received statement by clicking on ‘PREVIEW DRAFT TDS AND TCS CREDIT RECEIVED" button before filing.

items.q: Do I need to file TDS and TCS credit Received statement before filing of Form GSTR-1/3B?

spans.s: You may file the TDS and TCS credit Received statement before filing of Form GSTR-1/3B.

items.q: When ‘File TDS TCS credit received’ button will be enabled?

spans.s: Taxpayer needs to click on ‘Proceed to file’ button first. On click of this button, GST Portal will do necessary validations and “File TDS TCS credit received’ button will be enabled after such validations.

items.q: What are the modes of signing TDS and TCS Credit Received statement?

spans.s: You can file TDS and TCS Credit Received statement using DSC or EVC.
(a) Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)

Digital Signature Certificates (DSC) are the digital equivalent (that is electronic format) of physical or paper certificates. A digital certificate can be presented electronically to prove one’s identity, to access information or services on the Internet or to sign certain documents digitally. In India, DSC are issued by authorized Certifying Authorities.
 The GST Portal accepts only PAN based Class II and III DSC.
(b) Electronic Verification Code (EVC)

The Electronic Verification Code (EVC) authenticates the identity of the user at the GST Portal by generating an OTP. The OTP is sent to the mobile phone number of the registered mobile phone of Authorized Signatory filled in part A of the Registration Application.

items.q: What happens after TDS and TCS Credit Received statement is filed?
items.section: Post Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s: After TDS and TCS Credit received statement is filed:

items.q: What will be shown in the TCS Credit Received statement for older tax periods?
items.section: Post Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s:
For tax periods prior to April 2025, where data for Place of Supply (POS) is unavailable, the POS column will display ‘NA’.
 [Reference: GSTR-8 POS column inclusion via Notification No. 09/2025–Central Tax dated 11.02.2025]

items.q: Is it mandatory to add Remarks while accepting the records in TCS credit received /Amendment to TCS credit received table?
items.section: Post Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s:
It is not mandatory to add remarks from the Remarks column while accepting the records. 
 But it is mandatory to select remarks (reason for rejection) from the Remarks column while rejecting the records in TCS credit received /Amendment to TCS credit received tables.
 Following remarks will be available under Remarks dropdown list.
Please note that if you have selected
Others(Specify)
option from the
Remarks

dropdown list, you have to type the reason (within 100 characters) in the text box.
 The remarks selected by supplier while rejecting the records will be displayed in Table 4 (Amendment to TCS Details) - Rejected by Supplier tab of Form GSTR 8.

items.q: What is the process when an amended TDS or TCS record is auto-populated?
items.section: Post Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s: Amended records, based on GSTR-7 (for TDS) or GSTR-8 (for TCS), are auto-populated in the respective Amendment tables in the credit received statement. The supplier must Accept or Reject the amended records. Once accepted and filed, the credit is reflected in the Electronic Cash Ledger.

items.q: What are the sources of records in the Amendment to TCS/TDS Credit Received table?
items.section: Post Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s:
Amendments made by the e-commerce operator in Table 4 of GSTR-8 or by the deductor in Table 4 of GSTR-7.
 Rejected records that have been amended by the operator/deductor after rejection by the supplier.

items.q: What if the operator or deductor amends a record before the supplier acts on it?
items.section: Post Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s: The earlier auto-populated record will be freezed (i.e., disabled for action). The amended record will be auto-populated in the same TDS and TCS Credit statement or if filed than next open tax period statement for action by the supplier.

items.q: Can the same TCS or TDS record be accepted or rejected multiple times in Form GSTR-2X?
items.section: Post Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s:
No. A TCS or TDS record in Form GSTR-2X can be acted upon only once in respect of acceptance or rejection.
 Where a record is accepted, it becomes locked and cannot be amended or reversed by the deductor/collector in GSTR-7 or GSTR-8.
 Where no action is taken on a record in GSTR-2X, the deductor/collector may amend such record once in GSTR-7 or GSTR-8. Thereafter, only the amended version will be available in GSTR-2X for action.
 Where a record is rejected in GSTR-2X, the deductor/collector may make multiple amendments until it is finally accepted. Each fresh amendment will flow into the GSTR-2X of the tax period in which such amendment is filed, and the supplier/deductee can take action only on the latest record.

items.q: What happens after rejecting an amended TDS or TCS record?
items.section: Post Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s: The rejected record flows back to the respective return—Table 4 (Rejected by Deductee) of GSTR-7 (for TDS) or GSTR-8 (for TCS)—for further amendment by the deductor or e-commerce operator.

items.q: Can the entire statement be previewed before filing?
items.section: Post Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s: Yes. The taxpayer can click on the ‘PREVIEW DRAFT TDS AND TCS CREDIT RECEIVED’ button to download and review a PDF draft of the complete statement before filing.

items.q: How often can the TDS and TCS Credit Received statement be filed?
items.section: Post Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s: The statement can be filed only once for a given tax period and cannot be revised after filing. Filing of the TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement is neither mandatory nor sequential. However, once any record is accepted or rejected, the TDS and TCS Credit Statement for the subsequent month cannot be filed until the statement for the current month is submitted.

items.q: What appears in the TCS Credit Received statement post-POS update?
items.section: Post Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s: Multiple entries per e-commerce operator may be seen, each tagged with a different POS. Deductees must verify and act on each entry.

items.q: How can the TDS/TCS credit amount be used?
items.section: Post Filing of TDS and TCS Credit Received Statement

spans.s: It can be used to pay GST liabilities or claimed as refund. Composition taxpayers may use it to pay quarterly CMP-08 liabilities.

topics.title: Form GST ITC-03

items.q: What is Form GST ITC-03?

spans.s: Form GST ITC-03 is to be filled up by those taxpayers who opts for composition scheme or where goods or services or both supplied by taxpayer becomes wholly exempt. This form is to be filed by taxpayers, to pay an amount, by way of debit in the electronic credit ledger or electronic cash ledger, equivalent to credit availed in respect of:
• Inputs held in stock, and
• Inputs contained in semi-finished goods or finished goods held in stock, and
• Capital goods or plant and machinery

items.q: When filing of Form GST ITC-03 is needed for a taxpayer?

spans.s: In following conditions taxpayer must file Form GST ITC-03:
• Taxpayer has opted for composition scheme or goods or services or both supplied by a taxpayer becomes wholly exempt.
• Taxpayer has availed ITC in respect of input held in stock and input contained in semi-finished goods or finished goods held in stock and on capital goods or plant and machinery.

items.q: From where can I as taxpayer file Form GST ITC-03?

spans.s: Form GST ITC-03 can be accessed on the GST Portal, post login by the taxpayer.
The path is Services > Returns > ITC Forms.

items.q: What is the frequency for filing Form GST ITC-03?

spans.s: Registered person can file ‘Form GST ITC-03’ only once in a financial year for opting for composition scheme. For reversal/payment of tax in case of exemption of supplies it can be filed multiple times, as and when notifications exempting such supplies are issued by Government.

items.q: Can I preview the Form GST ITC-03 before filing?

spans.s: Yes, you can preview the Form GST ITC-03 before filing it on the GST Portal.

items.q: What is MAKE PAYMENT button for? What happens when MAKE PAYMENT button is clicked?

spans.s: MAKE PAYMENT
button is clicked to pay off the liabilities, computed based on details declared by the taxpayer. Once you click the
MAKE PAYMENT
button, liabilities are payed off and you cannot make any changes to Form GST ITC-03.

items.q: Why do I need to create a Challan?

spans.s: If available cash balance in Electronic Cash Ledger is less than the amount required to offset the liabilities; additional cash is required for paying the liabilities. You need to create the challan for that additional cash required, to offset the liabilities.

items.q: GST Portal has auto-populated the “Tax to be paid through ITC” fields. Can I edit the amount for ITC utilization?

spans.s: “Tax to be paid through ITC” fields show optimum credit utilization amounts by the GST Portal, based on provisions of the law/rules relating to credit utilization. However, you may edit the ITC utilization. As you change ITC utilization, the cash to be paid by you will also change.

items.q: What are the modes of signing Form GST ITC-03?

spans.s: You can file Form GST ITC-03 using DSC, or EVC.
Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)

Digital Signature Certificates (DSC) are the digital equivalent (that is electronic format) of physical or paper certificates. A digital certificate can be presented electronically to prove one’s identity, to access information or services on the Internet or to sign certain documents digitally. In India, DSC are issued by authorized Certifying Authorities.
The GST Portal accepts only PAN based Class II and III DSC.
Electronic Verification Code (EVC)

The Electronic Verification Code (EVC) authenticates the identity of the user at the GST Portal by generating an OTP. The OTP is sent to the mobile phone number of the registered mobile phone of Authorized Signatory filled in part A of the Registration Application.

items.q: What happens after Form GST ITC-03 is filed?

spans.s: After Form GST ITC-03 is filed:
• ARN will be generated in the GST portal and the same will be communicated to Taxpayer by SMS and E-mail, on their registered mobile number and e-mail id respectively.
• Balance of credit lying in Electronic Credit Ledger will lapse on filing of this form, after ITC reversal /payment of tax, in case of Opt-in for composition scheme.

items.q: Can I file Nil Form GST ITC-03?

spans.s: Yes, you can file Nil Form GST ITC-03.

items.q: When can I file Nil Form GST ITC-03?

spans.s: You can file Nil Form GST ITC-03, if you have -
(a) No stock of inputs or inputs contained in semi-finished and finished goods or capital goods on the day immediately preceding the day on which composition scheme has commenced; or

(b) The stock of inputs or inputs contained in semi-finished and finished goods or capital goods on the day immediately preceding the day on which composition scheme has commenced but you have not claimed input tax credit (ITC) on the same.

items.q: From where can I as taxpayer file Nil Form GST ITC-03?

spans.s: You can preview and file Nil Form GST ITC-03 by navigating to Services > Returns > ITC Forms option.
Note: You can preview Nil Form GST ITC-03 before filing.

items.q: What are the modes of signing Nil Form GST ITC-03?

spans.s: You can file Nil Form GST ITC-03 using DSC or EVC.
Note: Filling using DSC is mandatory for the class of taxpayers (Companies etc.) as specified in the rules.

items.q: What happens after Nil Form GST ITC-03 is filed?

spans.s: After Nil Form GST ITC-03 is filed, ARN will be generated in the GST Portal and the same will be communicated to taxpayer by SMS and E-mail, on their registered mobile number and e-mail id respectively.

topics.title: Form GST ITC-04

items.q: What is Form GST ITC-04?

spans.s: Form GST ITC-04 is a declaration form to be furnished by registered persons (Principal), showing the details of inputs or capital goods dispatched to or received from a job worker in a particular quarter.
The details of the following 4 types of transactions need to be furnished in GST ITC-04:
a) Inputs or capital goods dispatched to job workers in the quarter
b) Inputs or capital goods received back from job workers in the quarter
c) Inputs or capital goods sent from one job worker to another in the quarter
d) Inputs or capital goods supplied from the premises of job workers in the quarter

items.q: Who is required to file Form GST ITC-04?

spans.s: A registered manufacturer (Principal) is required to file “Form GST ITC-04’ on a quarterly basis, if such person is sending any inputs or capital goods to a job worker (both registered and unregistered), without payment of tax and receives it back or sends it out to another job worker or supplies from the premises of job worker to a customer directly.

items.q: Is it mandatory to file Form GST ITC-04?

spans.s: Yes, it is mandatory to file Form GST ITC-04 for a registered manufacturer (Principal), if he/she is sending any inputs or capital goods to a job worker and receives it back or sends it out to another job worker or supplies from the premises of job worker.

items.q: What are the modes of filing Form GST ITC-04?
items.section: Modes of Filing Form GST ITC-04

spans.s: The Form GST ITC-04 can be filed either in online mode directly or by using offline excel utility.

items.q: From where can I as a taxpayer can file Form GST ITC-04 online and offline?
items.section: Modes of Filing Form GST ITC-04

spans.s: Taxpayer can access Form GST ITC-04 by navigating to
Services
Returns
ITC Forms
after logging into the GST portal.
For filing Form GST ITC-04 offline, you can click
here
to know more.

items.q: What is the frequency for filing Form GST ITC-04?
items.section: Due Date of Filing Form GST ITC-04

spans.s:
Form GST ITC-04 is required to be filed on a quarterly basis for tax periods until September 2021. However, with effect from 1st October 2021, it is required to be filed on half yearly or annual basis depending upon the aggregate turnover of preceding financial year:
 (1) Those with an annual aggregate turnover of more than Rs.5 crore – Half-yearly from April-September- and October-March.
 (2) Those with an annual aggregate turnover of up to Rs.5 crore – Yearly from FY 2022-23.

items.q: What is the due date for filing Form GST ITC-04?
items.section: Due Date of Filing Form GST ITC-04

spans.s:
ITC-04 was to be filled on a quarterly basis for tax periods until September 2021.. It had to be furnished on or before the 25th day of the month succeeding the quarter. For example, for the Jul-Sept quarter, the due date was 25th October 2021.
 Those filing ITC-04 from October 2021 onwards are required to file it half yearly or yearly. If you have an annual aggregate turnover of more than Rs.5 crore, then you have to file it on half-yearly basis from April-September- due on 25th October and October-March- due on 25th April. If you have an annual aggregate turnover of up to Rs.5 crore, you have to file it annually from FY 2022-23 onwards due on 25th of the following month.

items.q: What is the late fee for filing Form GST ITC-04 after due date?
items.section: Due Date of Filing Form GST ITC-04

spans.s: As of now, there is no late fee, penalty or interest for late filing of Form GST ITC-04.

items.q: What are the details required to be provided in GST ITC-04?

spans.s: Details for following tables of Form GST ITC-04 are to be entered by registered persons (Principal):

items.q: Can I preview Form GST ITC-04 before filing?

spans.s: No, there is no option to preview Form GST ITC-04 before filing.

items.q: What are the modes of signing Form GST ITC-04?

spans.s: You can file Form GST ITC-04 using DSC or EVC.

topics.title: GST ITC-01

items.q: What is GST ITC-01?

spans.s: Registered person who is entitled to claim credit of input tax under section 18 (1) is required to file a declaration in Form ‘GST ITC-01’. The credit may be availed for inputs held in stock, inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock or capital goods as mentioned below:

items.q: Input Tax Credit can be availed on which goods?

spans.s: Input tax credit can be availed on following goods:

items.q: When can I claim Input Tax Credit?

spans.s: Registered person can claim credit of the inputs tax in respect of eligible stock of goods within 30 days from the date of becoming eligible to avail ITC under sub-section (1) of section 18 or within such further period as may be extended by the Commissioner:

items.q: By when do I need to claim Input Tax Credit?

spans.s: The input tax credit can be claimed for invoices up to one year prior to the date of grant of approval /opting out of composition scheme or exempt supplies becoming taxable and will be counted on or after appointed day. For capital goods the invoices can be dated 5 years prior to the date of grant of approval /opting out of composition scheme or exempt supplies becoming taxable.

items.q: What are the pre-conditions to claim Input Tax Credit?

spans.s: The claim in Form GST ITC-01 should be filed by the registered person within a period of thirty days from the date of becoming eligible to avail the input tax credit in terms of Section 18 of the Act. If the declared amount of ITC is more than Rs. 2 Lakh, then the details given in Form GST ITC-01 should be certified by practicing CA/Cost Accountant.

items.q: What will happen once the Form GST ITC-01 is filed?

spans.s: Once the Form GST ITC-01 is successfully filed, the amount of ITC claimed would be posted to your credit ledger; ARN is generated and SMS and Email are sent to the taxpayer.

topics.title: GST ITC-02A

items.q: What is Form GST ITC-02A?

spans.s: A person having multiple places of business in a State or Union territory may be granted separate registration for each place of business.

If a registered person, who has obtained separate registration for multiple places of business in a State/UT and intends to transfer unutilized matched Input Tax Credit lying in his/her Electronic Credit Ledger of an existing entity (the transferor entity) to newly registered entities/place of businesses (transferee entity), then transferor entity (existing entity) has to file Form GST ITC-02A on GST Portal, within 30 days from obtaining such registration and transferee entity (newly registered entity) can accept or reject the same.

items.q: When filing of Form GST ITC-02A is needed for a taxpayer?

spans.s: Taxpayer can file Form GST ITC-02A, if he/she has obtained separate registration for multiple places of business in a State/UT and intends to transfer unutilized matched Input Tax Credit lying in his/her Electronic Credit Ledger to registered entities/place of businesses.

items.q: From where can I as taxpayer transfer ITC in Form GST ITC-02A?
items.section: Transferring ITC in Form GST ITC-02A

spans.s: You can transfer ITC in Form GST ITC-02A by navigating to
Services
Returns
ITC Forms > TRANSFER ITC
after logging into the GST Portal.
Post filing of Form GST ITC-02A, Electronic Credit Ledger of transferor entity will get updated with a debit entry for the amount mentioned in the Form.

items.q: By when can I transfer ITC in Form GST ITC-02A?
items.section: Transferring ITC in Form GST ITC-02A

spans.s: As a transferor entity (existing entity), in case you have obtained separate registration for multiple places of business in a State/UT, you can transfer ITC in ‘Form GST ITC-02A’ within 30 days after obtaining such registration.

items.q: From where can I as transferee entity take action in Form GST ITC-02A?
items.section: Taking Action in Form GST ITC-02A

spans.s: You as transferee entity (newly registered entity), can take action in Form GST ITC-02A by navigating to
Services
Returns
ITC Forms > TAKE ACTION
after logging into the GST Portal.

items.q: What actions can be taken by the transferee entity in Form GST ITC-02A?
items.section: Taking Action in Form GST ITC-02A

spans.s: Transferee entity can accept or reject the ITC transferred by the transferor entity.

items.q: Can a Transferee entity modify the amount transferred by the transferor entity?
items.section: Taking Action in Form GST ITC-02A

spans.s: Transferee entity cannot modify the amount transferred by the transferor entity.

items.q: What happens after Form GST ITC-02A is successfully filed by the transferor entity?
