items.q: Is it mandatory to authenticate Aadhaar or upload e-KYC documents for filing application for Revocation of Cancelled Registration?

spans.s: If cancelled taxpayer’s Aadhaar is not already authenticated, it would be mandatory to authenticate Aadhar or upload e-KYC documents (which must mandatorily include Aadhaar enrolment ID), for filing application for Revocation of Cancelled Registration.

topics.title: Applying for Cancellation of Enrolment by GST Practitioner

items.q: Can a GST Practitioner file an application for cancellation of enrolment?

spans.s: Yes, a GST Practitioner can file an application for cancellation of enrolment.

items.q: From where can I apply for cancellation of enrolment?

spans.s: Navigate to Services > Registration > Application for Cancellation of Enrolment option to apply for cancellation of enrolment.

items.q: Is it mandatory to give reasons for cancellation of enrolment?

spans.s: Yes, it is mandatory to give at-least one reason for cancellation of enrolment in the Reason for Cancellation field.

items.q: What is the process to file an application for cancellation of enrolment and processing by the Tax Official?

spans.s: Listed below is the process to file an application for cancellation of enrolment and processing by the Tax Official:
1. GST Practitioner can surrender their enrolment by applying cancellation application on GST Portal by navigating to Services > Registration > Application for Cancellation of Enrolment option.
2. On successfully filing the application for cancellation of enrolment, application will be sent to the Tax Official for processing who can raise SCN, approve or reject the application.

2.1 In case of SCN raise by Tax Official: GST Practitioner can reply to the notice by navigating to Services > Registration > Application for Filing Clarifications option within 7 working days of receiving the notice.
2.2 In case of approval by Tax Official: Once the application for cancellation of enrolment of a GST Practitioner is approved by the Tax Official:

items.s: GST Practitioner will get a confirmation of the cancellation of enrolment on their registered e-mail address and mobile number.
An e-mail is sent to all the taxpayers which are assigned to such GST Practitioner stating that the particular GST Practitioner has been cancelled.
GST Practitioner will not be able to engage/disengage any taxpayer and perform any activities on their behalf.

spans.s: 2.3 In case of rejection by Tax Official: Once the application for cancellation of enrolment of a GST Practitioner is rejected by the Tax Official:

items.s: GST Practitioner will get a confirmation of the rejection of application for cancellation of enrolment on their registered e-mail address and mobile number.
GST Practitioner will not be able to engage/disengage any taxpayer and perform any activities on their behalf.

items.q: Can I file for amendment of Core fields after applying for cancellation of enrolment?
items.section: Amendment of Core and Non-Core Fields

spans.s: No. Once you have submitted the application for cancellation of enrolment, and ARN has been generated, you will not be allowed to file for amendment of Core fields.

items.q: Can I file for amendment of Non-Core fields after applying for cancellation of enrolment?
items.section: Amendment of Core and Non-Core Fields

spans.s: Yes, even after you have submitted an application for cancellation of enrolment, and ARN has been generated, you can still file for amendment of Non-Core fields.

items.q: Why is the Submit button in form for cancellation of enrolment not getting active despite filling it out?

spans.s: The Submit button gets activated once all the mandatory fields (other than signatures) are filled. Please check all the mandatory fields carefully and provide information for any field that you might have missed.

items.q: What will happen once cancellation of enrolment is submitted by the GST Practitioner?

spans.s: On successfully filing the application for cancellation of enrolment:

items.q: I have submitted application for cancellation of enrolment. From where can I view the status of the submitted application?

spans.s: GST Practitioner can view the status of the submitted application under Services > User Services > View My Submissions option.

items.q: From where can I reply to the SCN issued by the Tax Official?
items.section: Order Issued by the Tax Official

spans.s: You can reply to the SCN issued by the Tax Official by navigating to Services > Registration > Application for Filing Clarifications option.

items.q: What will happen once the application for cancellation for enrolment of a GST Practitioner is approved by the Tax Official?
items.section: Order Issued by the Tax Official

spans.s: Once the application for cancellation of enrolment of a GST Practitioner is approved by the Tax Official:

items.s: GST Practitioner will get a confirmation of the cancellation of enrolment on their registered e-mail address and mobile number.
An e-mail is sent to all the taxpayers which are assigned to such GST Practitioner stating that the particular GST Practitioner has been cancelled.
GST Practitioner will not be able to engage/disengage any taxpayer and perform any activities on their behalf.

items.q: What will happen once the application for cancellation for enrolment of a GST Practitioner is rejected by the Tax Official?
items.section: Order Issued by the Tax Official

spans.s: Once the application for cancellation of enrolment of a GST Practitioner is rejected by the Tax Official:

items.s: GST Practitioner will get a confirmation of the rejection of application for cancellation of enrolment on their registered e-mail address and mobile number.
GST Practitioner will be able to engage/disengage any taxpayer and perform any activities on their behalf.

items.q: From where can I view the order issued by the Tax Official?
items.section: Order Issued by the Tax Official

spans.s: GST Practitioner can view the issued order under Services > User Services > View Notices and Orders option.

items.q: How am I intimated about cancellation of enrolment?

spans.s: You will get a confirmation of the cancellation of enrolment on your registered e-mail address and mobile number.

items.q: Will the taxpayers to whom I am assigned as GST Practitioner be intimated about cancellation of enrolment?

spans.s: Once enrolment of a GSTP is cancelled, an email is sent to the all the taxpayers which are assigned to such GST Practitioner stating that the particular GST Practitioner has been cancelled.

topics.title: Advance Ruling for Unregistered Dealers (FORM GST ARA-01)

items.q: Who can I apply for Advance Ruling?

spans.s: Application for Advance Ruling can be filed by any person who is registered or is desirous of obtaining registration under this Act on the matters prescribed under the GST Act with payment of the prescribed fee.
The process for filing advance ruling application by an unregistered taxpayer is different from that for a registered taxpayer.
Click here to know more about how to apply for seeking advance ruling by registered taxpayer.

items.q: What is the process to apply for seeking Advance Ruling by unregistered dealers?

spans.s: 1. Unregistered applicant accesses the GST Portal and creates a Temporary User ID on GST Portal.
Click
here
to know more about how to create a Temporary ID.
2. Applicant logs in to the GST Portal using the Temporary User ID.
Click
here
to know more about how to login to the GST Portal for the first time.
3. Applicant creates Challan after logging to the GST Portal for payment of prescribed fee.
Click
here
to know more about how to create Challan.
4. Challan must be duly paid and Challan Receipt along with Challan Identification Number (CIN) must also be obtained.
5. Applicant downloads the advance ruling form, from the GST Portal, and fills the same along with the temporary User ID and Challan receipt and submits it manually at the Tax Office. Navigate to
Downloads
Offline Tools
GST ARA 01 - Application for Advance Ruling
to download the offline tool.

items.q: On what matters an applicant can file an application for Advance Ruling?

spans.s: Application for Advance Ruling can be filed on the following matters, as prescribed under the CGST/SGST/IGST Act.
a) Classification of any goods or services or both;
b) Applicability of a notification issued under the provisions of the Act;
c) Determination of time and value of supply of goods or services or both;
d) Admissibility of input tax credit of tax paid or deemed to have been paid;
e) Determination of the liability to pay tax on any goods or services or both;
f) Whether applicant is required to be registered;
g) Whether any particular thing done by the applicant with respect to any goods or services or both amounts to or results in a supply of goods or services or both, within the meaning of that term.

items.q: I am a Non-Resident, Can I apply for the Advance Ruling?

spans.s: Yes, in case a non-resident wants to file Advance Ruling application, then he/she can login into the portal by creating temporary user ID or with the GST Portal credentials, if already registered as a Non Resident Taxpayer (NRTP). However, all the communications in the form of email shall be sent on the email id of the authorized signatory, whose details were provided at the time of generation of User Id.

items.q: How an unregistered person can intimate about the payment made?

spans.s: An unregistered person creates a challan and after making payment, need to take the print of that challan (along with other documents) to State Advance Ruling Authority Office. The login facility is not provided to Unregistered Taxpayer. However unregistered person can register on GST Portal as explained in Question no 2.

items.q: Can I track the status of my payment for the Advance Ruling?

spans.s: Yes, you can navigate to
Services
Payments
Track Payment Status
command to track the status of payment for Advance Ruling.

items.q: Can I provide the other supporting documents along with the application?

spans.s: Yes, you can upload the relevant supporting documents which you are required to submit along with the application form. However, you can upload only 4 documents with the maximum size of 5 MB each and the remaining documents can be handed over in hard copy. In case, the Authority requires further documents, you can provide the necessary documents at the time of Personal Hearing.

topics.title: Filing an application (FORM GST ARA-01) for seeking Advance Ruling by Registered Taxpayers and Tracking or Taking Action in the Subsequent Proceedings

items.q: Who can apply for Advance Ruling?

spans.s: An application for Advance Ruling can be filed by a registered taxpayers as well as an unregistered persons. However, in case of an unregistered user, the application can be filed after getting a temporary ID for Advance Ruling.
Click here
to know more about how to create a Temporary ID for Advance Ruling.

items.q: On what matters we can file an application for Advance Ruling?

spans.s: A registered person as well as any other person desirous of obtaining registration can apply for Advance Ruling on the following matters, as prescribed under the act with the prescribed fee.
a) Classification of any goods or services or both;
b) Applicability of a notification issued under the provisions of this Act;
c) Determination of time and value of supply of goods or services or both;
d) Admissibility of input tax credit of tax paid or deemed to have been paid;
e) Determination of the liability to pay tax on any goods or services or both;
f) Whether applicant is required to be registered;
g) Whether any particular thing done by the applicant with respect to any goods or services or both amounts to or results in a supply of goods or services or both, within the meaning of that term.

items.q: What are the pre-condition for applying the Advance Ruling by a registered taxpayer?

spans.s: 1. Applicant wants to obtain Advance Ruling in respect of any specified matter(s) from the Authority.
2. Registered applicant has obtained registration (GSTIN) on the GST portal.
3. Applicant has deposited fee amount in his Electronic Cash Ledger.

items.q: What is the process to apply for seeking Advance Ruling? OR What steps must be followed to seek hearing for Advance Ruling?

spans.s: 1. Applicant logs in to the GST Portal and navigate to Services > User Services > My Applications command..
2. Select the Application Type as Advance Ruling from the drop-down list and click the NEW APPLICATION button.

3. If there is no sufficient balance in Cash Ledger under Fee head and “Amount to be paid” is not nil, then click Deposit in Cash Ledger button to deposit the required amount in Cash Ledger. If taxpayer has sufficient balance in Cash Ledger under Fee head, click CREATE APPLICATION FOR ADVANCE RULING.
4. Fill the required details in the application form.
5. Click Download Template to download the template for Advance Ruling Application,
6. Update the template with required information.
7. Under Details of Advance Ruling Application, upload, click the Choose file button. Navigate and select the Filled template.
8. Under Upload Supporting Documents, enter Document Description and click the Choose File button. Navigate and select the Supporting Documents.
9. Under Verification Tab, enter the details.
10. Click PREVIEW to preview the Application before filing,
11. After filling the enrolment application, you need to digitally sign the application using Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)/ E-Signature or EVC.
12. Once the Verification is completed, fee amount will be auto debited from the cash ledger and ARN will be generated and status is changed to Filed.

items.q: Under which acts fee is to be paid for filing Advance Ruling Application by normal and OIDAR taxpayer?

spans.s: Note
: The respective amount, to be paid, will be auto calculated based on selection of SGST/CGST/IGST heads, as the case may be.

items.q: On what basis should I select Nature of business activities?

spans.s: Applicant need to select the nature of business activity(s) in which Advance Ruling is sought. Applicant can also select multiple nature of business activity(s) if required.

items.q: Can I provide the other supporting documents along with the application?

spans.s: Yes, applicant can upload relevant supporting documents which he is required to submit along with the application form. However, he can upload only 4 documents with the maximum size of 5 MB each, the remaining documents can be handed over in hard copy. In case the Authority requires further documents, Applicant can provide the necessary documents at the time of Personal Hearing.

items.q: Can I track the status of my application for the Advance Ruling?

spans.s: Yes, after successful submission of application, ARN will get generated along with Acknowledgement. Applicant can view the status from “My Applications” menu under “User Services” tab available on the dashboard, using the ARN and submission period.
Navigate to
Services

Track Payment Status
command to track the status of application for Advance Ruling.

items.q: What do I need to do after filing an Advance Ruling Application on the GST Portal?

spans.s: Applicants, after filing an application, need to participate in the related proceedings and take necessary actions as intimated by AAR or AAAR.

On the GST Portal, for ease of all Applicants, details of each Application filed by the taxpayer is organized into the following six tabs in the Case Details Screen: APPLICATIONS, NOTICES, REPLIES, ORDERS, RECTIFICATION and ADDITIONAL DOCUMENT. Applicant can easily access these tabs of an Application to track all proceedings related to that particular application and take necessary actions.

items.q: What actions can I take if AAR rejects my Application for seeking Advance Ruling?

spans.s: Once AAR rejects an Application for seeking Advance Ruling, the Applicant can file an application for Rectification using "File Rectification" link on the ORDERS tab.

items.q: Can I file an Appeal on the GST Portal if AAR rejects my Application for seeking Advance Ruling?

spans.s: No, you cannot file an appeal on the GST Portal if AAR rejects your Application for seeking Advance Ruling.

items.q: What are the steps involved in Processing of an Admitted Application for seeking Advance Ruling?

spans.s: Once the AAR issues an order admitting the Application for seeking Advance Ruling, following steps take place:
a. In case of concurrence, AAR shall issue order disposing the Advance Ruling Application. Status of the ARN is changed from "Pending For Order" to “Disposed by Authority”.

b. In case of difference of Opinion among the AAR Members, AAR shall refer the case to AAAR. AAR can make partial reference or complete reference. Partial reference is made if there is partial difference of opinion among the AAR Members. In this case, both Order and Reference is made. Order is passed in regards of concurrent points and Reference is made to AAAR on non-concurrent points. In both the cases, Status of the ARN is changed from “Disposed by Authority” to "
Referred by Authority".

items.q: What actions take place on the GST Portal once AAAR disposes my Application (referred by AAR) for seeking Advance Ruling?

spans.s: Once AAAR disposes the Application for seeking Advance Ruling, following actions take place on the GST Portal:

items.q: What actions can I take once AAAR disposes my Application (referred by AAR) for seeking Advance Ruling?

spans.s: Once AAAR disposes the Application for seeking Advance Ruling, the Applicant can file an application for Rectification (if the nature of order is such that it requires rectification) using "File Rectification" link on the ORDERS tab.

items.q: What is Rectification of an Order?

spans.s: Rectification of an Order is correcting mistake(s) in the order passed under Section 98 or 101 respectively by the AAR or AAAR.

Note: If the rectification has the effect of enhancing the tax liability or reducing the amount of admissible input tax credit, the AAR/AAAR shall make the rectification only after giving a notice and a reasonable opportunity of being heard to the Applicant.

items.q: From where can I file application for Rectification of an Order?

spans.s: Once AAR/AAAR disposes an Application related to Advance Ruling, the Applicant can file an application for Rectification using "File Rectification" link on the ORDERS tab.

items.q: Will the system allow me to file Rectification even after 6 months of the issue of that Order?

spans.s: In case the difference between the date of the order and rectification application filed is more than 6 months, the information message will pop up asking for confirmation if you still want to file the Rectification Application as the period exceeds 6 months from the date of the order. In case, you select “YES”, System will allow you to proceed with the application. In case, you select “NO”, System will bring you back to the earlier screen.

items.q: What are the steps involved in Processing of an Application for Rectification of Advance Ruling?

spans.s: Following steps are involved in Processing of an Application for Rectification of Advance Ruling:
If Rectification is filed by a Taxpayer or CO/JO:
AAR/AAAR reviews the Application and can take the following actions:

i. Issue "Rejection of Rectification Application" Order, with reasons for rejection: If the AAR/AAAR is satisfied that the rectification is not required or the application is time barred, it will provide an opportunity of being heard and issue "Hearing Notice" for Acceptance/Rejection of Rectification Application to the Applicant and CO and/or JO, with date, place and time of hearing. Based on the hearing, it will pass the Order. Also, Status of the ARN is updated to "Rectification Rejected". The parties (i.e. the applicant and the jurisdictional officer and/or concerned officer) will be informed about such order through email.
ii. Proceed with Rectification:
If Suo moto Rectification is done by AAR/AAAR:

CASE 1 - In case opportunity of being heard is required because the rectification has the effect of enhancing the tax liability or reducing the amount of admissible input tax credit, following steps take place:

CASE 2 - In case opportunity of being heard is not required, AR/AAAR will rectify the order. Status of the ARN is updated to "Application Disposed". The parties (i.e. the applicant and the jurisdictional officer and/or concerned officer or AAR, if Order is rectified by AAAR) will be informed about such order through email.

items.q: Once AAR/AAAR initiates Rectification proceedings or CO/JO files Application for Rectification of Order, will I receive its auto-intimation?

spans.s: Yes, once AAR/AAAR initiates Rectification proceedings or CO/JO files Application for Rectification of Order, GST portal will automatically send you an email informing about receipt of the application of Rectification of Order or Suo moto initiation of Rectification along with Rectification Reference Number and application date.

items.q: How many Applications of Rectifications of Order can I file?

spans.s: Application for rectification of the order can be filed multiple times.

items.q: Once CO/JO files a Counter Reply, will I receive its auto-intimation?

spans.s: Yes, once CO/JO files a Counter Reply, GST portal will automatically send you an email informing about receipt of the Counter Reply, along with Reply Reference Number and Reply date.

items.q: Can I submit more than one Reply to a Notice?

spans.s: No, you cannot submit more than one Reply to a Notice. Once the reply is submitted, the Reply link in the NOTICES tab will get disabled. In case you want to modify your reply or submit any additional documents, you can do so during Personal Hearing and submit the hardcopy of the documents. These additional documents will be uploaded by the tax official on the GST Portal.

items.q: What actions take place on the GST Portal once I file a Reply?

spans.s: Once you file a reply, following actions take place on the GST Portal:
·  REPLIES tab is automatically updated with a table containing details of the reply.
·  A Reference Number is generated and is sent to you through an email. Also, intimation for submission of the reply is sent to the Jurisdictional Officer / Concerned Officer through an email.

items.q: Is there a limit on Adjournments, during Processing of all Applications related to Advance Ruling?

spans.s: There is no limit on Adjournments. Hearing can be adjourned any no. of times.

items.q: Can I file an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order passed by AAR, in case of Partial reference?

spans.s: Yes, in case of Partial reference also, Appeal can be filed against the Advance Ruling Order passed by Authority for Advance Ruling.

items.q: Do I need to deposit any fee to file an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order passed by AAR?

spans.s: Yes, you need to deposit the applicable fee to file an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order passed by AAR. The applicable fee will be displayed on the New Application page once you initiate filing of Appeal against Advance Ruling. Without depositing the required fee you won't be able to proceed further and file appeal.

items.q: I am filing an Appeal on 01/04/2018 against the Advance Ruling Order passed by AAR on 01/03/2018. Do I need to need to attach the Details of Condonation of Delay (COD) along with the Appeal Application?

spans.s: Yes, you need to attach the Details of Condonation of Delay (COD) along with the Appeal Application. This is because the number of days delay in filing Appeal is calculated after expiry of 30 days and in your case the number of days delay in filing Appeal is ‘1’. This will be displayed in No. of days delay in filing appeal field of the Advance Ruling Appeal Application screen when you initiate filing of appeal.

Orders issued by AAR:

items.q: Against which all Orders issued by AAR can I file an Appeal?

spans.s: You can file an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order and Rectification Order (in case the Advance Ruling Order is rectified) issued by AAR.

items.q: What actions take place once I file an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order passed by AAR?

spans.s: Following actions take place on the GST Portal after successful filing of an Appeal Application against the Advance Ruling Order passed by AAR:
1. ARN gets generated along with Acknowledgement and is communicated to the Appellant through an email and SMS.
2. An email is sent to the Concerned officer and Jurisdictional Officer informing them about receipt of application along with ARN and application date.
3. Appellant can navigate to Dashboard > Services > User Services > My Applications and search for the Application and open the Case Details Screen. Status of the ARN will be "Pending for Order"
4. The application will land in the AAAR's queue under Application inbox and will be available to Registrar, Authority Members and Steno and Appeal Proceedings will follow.

items.q: What actions take place once Concerned Officer or Jurisdictional Officer files an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order passed by AAR?

spans.s: Following actions take place on the GST Portal after successful filing of an Appeal Application against the Advance Ruling Order passed by AAR:

items.q: Once I file an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order passed by AAR, to whom all GST Portal will send its auto-intimation?

spans.s: Once you file an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order passed by AAR, GST portal will automatically send an acknowledgement email and SMS to the Appellant and email intimation to the jurisdictional officer and Concerned Officer informing about receipt of appeal application along with ARN and application date.

items.q: Once CO/JO files an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order passed by AAR, will I receive its auto-intimation?

spans.s: Yes, once CO/JO files an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order passed by AAR, GST portal will automatically send you an email informing about receipt of appeal application along with ARN and application date.

items.q: Can I file an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order after 60 days without COD?

spans.s: Yes, Appeal can be filed even after 30 days and up to 60 days (even without COD) or even after 60 days from the date of communication of the order appeal against. In case of delay, please attach the Application for COD in “Upload Supporting Document” section of the Appeal Application.

items.q: Can I file an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order which is modified or issued by AAAR (in case of Reference)?

spans.s: No, you cannot file an Appeal against the Advance Ruling Order which is modified or issued by AAAR (in case of Reference)

items.q: What are the steps involved in Processing of an Appeal Application against Advance Ruling?

spans.s: Following are the key-steps of the Proceedings related to an Appeal Application:
If COD is required:

(i) Issue "Acceptance of Condonation of Delay" Order if AAAR is satisfied that the Appellant was prevented by sufficient cause to present the appeal within 30 days from the date of the communication of the order of the AAR. Also, he/she may allow appeal for a further period of 30 days and condone the delay upto a period of 30 days. In this case, its intimation is sent by a system-generated email to the Appellant and Respondents and the Status of the ARN is changed from "Pending For Order" to “Admitted”.

(ii) Issue "Rejection of Condonation of Delay" Order if AAAR is not satisfied that the Appellant was prevented by sufficient cause to present the appeal within 30 days from the date of the communication of the order of the AAR or the delay period is more than 30 days. In this case, its intimation is sent by a system-generated email to the Appellant and Respondents and the Status of the ARN is changed from "Pending For Order" to “Rejected”.
If COD is not required or if COD is condoned and Appeal is admitted:

topics.title: Filing Declaration by GTA (Goods and Transport Agencies) taxpayers

items.q: What is Annexure V? Why do I need to file Annexure V Form?

spans.s: If you are providing a Good Transport Agencies (GTA) services and wish to opt for payment of tax on forward charge mechanism, you are required to file declaration in Annexure V Form, every year before the commencement of any financial year by the cut-off date.
Note
: The cut-off date for filing Annexure V Form is 15th March of the preceding financial year.

items.q: How can I file Annexure V Form?

spans.s: To file Annexure V Form, navigate to
Services
User Services
Opting Forward Charge Payment by GTA (Annexure V)
option after login.

items.q: The SIGN AND FILE WITH EVC button is not enabled. I am not able to click it. How will I proceed to the next step?

spans.s: After entering the name of authorised signatory and place only,
SIGN AND FILE WITH EVC
button will be enabled.

items.q: Is there any limitation on the validity of OTP and who will receive these OTPs?

spans.s: The validity period of each OTP is mentioned in the SMS and e-mail sent to you. They are valid for 10 minutes.
Note
Case I
: If Primary Authorized Signatory has signed the
Annexure V Form
using EVC, then the OTP will be sent only to the
Primary Authorized Signatory
Case II
: If Secondary Authorized Signatory has signed the
Annexure V Form
using EVC, then the OTP will be sent to both,
Primary
and

items.q: How long should I wait for the OTPs before clicking on the resend OTP button?

spans.s: One
OTP
will be generated and the same OTP will be shared to your
e-mail
and
mobile phone

Please wait for at least 180 seconds after generating the OTP.
 In case you have still not received the OTP, make sure you are checking the correct mobile phone and e-mail. For e-mail OTP, you must also check the spam folder of your e-mail account.
 In case you have still not received OTP on either device, please click on Click to
Resend OTP

option available on the screen and the OTP will be resent. 
 Please note, when you generate fresh OTP, the previous OTP received on mobile, and e-mail would become invalid.

items.q: I want to download the Annexure V form for the previous financial year. How can I download?

spans.s: To download the Annexure V Form filed for the previous FY, select the financial year from the drop-down menu and click
GO
button. Click
DOWNLOAD ANNEXURE V
button to download the filed form.
Note:

1. If you have not filed Annexure V Form for any Financial Year, but try to download for the said FY, then the error message will pop-up stating that “You have not filed Annexure V for the selected Financial Year”.
2. Option for filing Declaration in Annexure V Form is available on the portal from the Financial year 2023-24 onwards only.

items.q: I filed my declaration in Annexure V Form for the FY 2024-25. Am I required to file Annexure V every year?

spans.s: No, the declaration in Annexure V Form filed for any financial year will be deemed to be continued for the subsequent FYs until declaration in Annexure VI has been filed (for opting to revert to reverse charge payment).

items.q: What is Annexure VI? Why do I need to file Annexure VI Form?

spans.s: If you are providing a Good Transport Agencies (GTA) services and wish to opt for reverting to reverse charge mechanism for succeeding Financial Year, you are required to file declaration in Annexure VI Form.
Note
: The cut-off date for filing Annexure VI for succeeding financial year will be from 1st January to 31st March of previous financial year.

items.q: I am a newly registered taxpayer. What will be the due date for filing Annexure V?

spans.s: Newly registered taxpayers will be able to file a declaration in Annexure V in the Current Financial Year. The due date for such taxpayers will be 45 Days from the Date of Application or one month from the Date of Issuance of Registration Certificate whichever is later.
Note
: Due date will be automatically calculated by the system and the same will be displayed to the taxpayer on the dashboard, post login.

items.q: I filed my declaration in Annexure V Form for the FY 2023-24 manually with the jurisdiction office. Am I required to upload manually filed Annexure V?

spans.s: Yes. You are required to upload the acknowledged copy of the Annexure V Form filed in the Jurisdiction office so as the system will record your declaration and you will not require to file declaration in Annexure V Form for the subsequent financial years.
Note

:
 1. This is a onetime exercise required to be done by the GTA taxpayers who manually filed their declaration in Annexure V for the FY 2023-24 to record their declaration on the system for enabling their declaration to be deemed for the subsequent financial years or to allow filing declaration in Annexure VI for the subsequent financial years. This functionality to upload the manually filed Annexure V for the FY 2023-24 will be available on the portal only up to 31.03.2024.

2. GTA taxpayers who uploaded their acknowledged copy of manually filed Annexure V Form for the FY 2023-24, are not required to file Annexure V Declaration for the FY 2024-25 and onwards, if they wish to continue with payment on Forward Charge mechanism.

3. Only those GTA taxpayers who uploaded their acknowledged copy of manually filed Annexure V Form for the FY 2023-24 would be allowed to file their declaration in Annexure VI form for the FY 2024-25 and onwards, if they wish to revert to payment on Reverse Charge mechanism.

topics.title: View and Download Accounting and Billing Software

items.q: What is Accounting and Billing Software on the GST Portal?

spans.s: Accounting and Billing Software download functionality is made available for the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) having turnover less than Rs. 1.5 crores. This software allows a taxpayer to run his daily business by providing day to day billing and accounting features, alongwith facility for return filing for their GST related compliances.

The software would be available free of cost to eligible taxpayers till 31.03.2021 or till the taxpayer’s annual turnover remains under Rs 1.5 Cr in a financial year, after which the taxpayers may have to pay a fee to the vendor.  It may be noted that only certain basic features of the software would be provided free. Some of the free features being made available by all the vendors are Sale/ Purchase/ Cash ledger, Inventory management, Supplier/ Customer Masters, Generation of Invoices, Preparation of GST Returns etc.
For using features other than free features listed or using the software beyond the initial free period, the taxpayer may visit respective vendor product site to ascertain fee payable, if any.

items.q: Who can download Accounting and Billing Software on the GST Portal?

spans.s: Accounting and Billing Software download functionality is made available for the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) having turnover less than Rs. 1.5 crores.

items.q: From where can I download Accounting and Billing Software on the GST Portal?

spans.s: To download the accounting and billing software on the GST Portal, login to the GST Portal with valid credentials. Navigate to
Downloads > Accounting and Billing Software
option.

items.q: "Accounting and Billing Software" functionality on the GST Portal is available to which all type of taxpayers and in which States/UTs?

spans.s: “Accounting and Billing Software" functionality is only available to active Normal (Regular), taxpayers who have opted for composition scheme  and SEZ Developer/ SEZ Unit who are registered on the GST Portal, having turnover less than Rs. 1.5 crores in a financial year. The functionality is available to the taxpayers for all States/ UTs.

items.q: I am not able to view "Accounting and Billing Software" link on the GST Portal?

spans.s: "Accounting and Billing Software" download functionality is available to active Normal, taxpayers who have opted for composition scheme and SEZ Developer/ SEZ Unit registered on the GST Portal. "Accounting and Billing Software" download functionality is available to the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) having turnover less than Rs. 1.5 crores.

items.q: Is there any fee for usage of Accounting and Billing Software?
items.section: Fee for Accounting and Billing Software

spans.s: It may be noted that only certain basic features of the software would be provided free. Some of the free features being made available by all the vendors are Sale/ Purchase/ Cash ledger, Inventory management, Supplier/ Customer Masters, Generation of Invoices, Preparation of GST Returns etc. For using features other than free features listed or using the software beyond the initial free period, the taxpayer may visit respective vendor product site to ascertain fee payable, if any.

items.q: Is there any renewal required for usage of Accounting and Billing Software, after expiry of the fixed term?
items.section: Fee for Accounting and Billing Software

spans.s: The features as offered and indicated in the link are offered to persons of specified turnover, free of cost. For using features other than free features listed or using the software beyond the initial free period till 31.03.2021, the taxpayer may visit respective vendor product site to ascertain fee payable, if any.

to view the list of common features offered by the Accounting and Billing Software.

items.q: Is there any check for validating the annual turnover of the taxpayer opting for the Accounting and Billing Software as per Return filed on the GST Portal by them?
items.section: Fee for Accounting and Billing Software

spans.s: No, there is no check for validating the annual turnover of the taxpayer opting for the Accounting and Billing Software as per Return filed on the GST Portal by them. However, the declaration given by the taxpayer regarding the turnover would be captured and recorded on the GST Portal.

items.q: My turnover has exceeded 1.5 crore after I started using the Accounting and Billing Software. Will any legal action be taken against me for using the Accounting and Billing Software?
items.section: Fee for Accounting and Billing Software

spans.s: Please note that your use of Accounting and Billing Software will be governed by the licensing and terms and conditions of the respective Accounting and Billing Software vendor.

items.q: What is the Disclaimer given by GSTN in the Accounting and Billing Software?
items.section: Disclaimer of GSTN & Declaration by Taxpayer

spans.s: GSTN makes no representations or warranty whatsoever about the Account & Billing Software which you may access through
www.gstn.org

. When you access the software, please understand that it is independent from GSTN, and that GSTN has no control over that Software. GSTN does not endorse or accepts any responsibility the use/misuse by such Software. It is up to you to take necessary precautions. GSTN is not collecting taxpayers’ data through the Software in any manner. Please read the terms and conditions of the Software properly before proceeding forward.

topics.title: View/Change Annual Aggregate Turnover (AATO)

items.q: From where can I view Annual Aggregate Turnover (AATO) details?

spans.s: You can view Annual Aggregate Turnover (AATO) details on your dashboard, below the Ledger Balance, post login to the GST Portal.

items.q: How are the AATO details compiled?

spans.s: The AATO figures are compiled with a computation methodology based on Form GSTR-3B/ Form GSTR-4/ Form CMP-08. The compilation includes returns filed by the taxpayer of all GSTINs of the related PAN. You can click the
Click here
link to view the Turnover Calculation methodology.

items.q: For which type of taxpayers are the AATO details available?

spans.s: AATO details are available for the following class of taxpayers:
Normal Taxpayer
SEZ Unit/SEZ Developer
Composition Taxpayer

items.q: How can I update the Annual Aggregate Turnover (AATO) details?

spans.s: To update the Annual Aggregate Turnover (AATO) details, navigate to
Dashboard
, select the previous
Financial Year
from the drop down and click
View/Update
button under
Estimated
column.
Note

: The taxpayer have an option to View their AATO for the current financial year also. However the option to update the AATO becomes available only after the due date of filing of return for the last month of the FY is over.

items.q: Why are the taxpayers required to update their AATO?

spans.s: Government is taking most of the policy decisions based on the aggregate turnover of a taxpayer including filing returns, composition option, and relief in late fee, and interest during COVID period or otherwise due to any other exigency.

items.q: When can I update my turnover details? What happens if I fail to update it in the prescribed period?

spans.s: The period of turnover updation usually falls after the due date of last return for the previous financial year gets over in April month of the subsequent FY. The time period given for Turnover Update is one month within which the taxpayer can update the turnover twice. The exact dates may vary based on the due date of the return filing for the last month/quarter of the Previous FY. In case you don’t update the turnover within the said period, the turnover calculated by the system, displayed on the Taxpayer’s dashboard will be considered as final.

items.q: How many times can I amend/update the turnover details?

spans.s: You can update the turnover twice during the aforementioned period of one month, after which the
Update
button will be disabled.

items.q: What happens if the change in AATO as a result of taxpayer’s turnover update, is either decreased or increased by 20% or more and/or the aggregate turnover is either decreased or increased so as to cross Rs. 5 Crore threshold over the system calculated AATO?

spans.s: In both the aforementioned scenarios, the taxpayer’s turnover update will be compulsorily sent for the jurisdictional tax officer’s review. The tax officer will have an option to amend the turnover updated by the taxpayer and in such cases the amended turnover shall be treated as Final AATO.

items.q: When can I view the Final Approved Turnover after I have updated the Final Turnover Declaration in the Portal? Also what is the Difference between the Final Approved Turnover and Final Turnover Declaration?

spans.s:
You can view Final Annual Aggregate Turnover after the end of subsequent month in which the taxpayer had updated their turnover details on the GST Portal after it has been approved by tax officer. In Case no update has been made by the taxpayer, the system calculated AATO shall be considered as final
 Final Turnover Declaration is the Turnover value reported by the Tax Payer while Final Approved Turnover is the Final Turnover visible to the Tax Payer after the updating by the Tax Officer or based on the Declaration done by the Tax Payer.

items.q: If the updated TO of taxpayers does not falls in the category of 20% or 5 Cr, can it be revised by Tax officer?

spans.s: No, it will not go to the Tax Officer. The value updated by the Tax Payer will be considered as Final.

items.q: When can I view Final Approved Turnover and Final Turnover Declaration after it has been sent to tax officer?

spans.s: You can view Final Approved Turnover 1st July onwards, after it has been approved by tax officer or if no update has been made by tax officer in the turnover and you can view Final Turnover Declaration 1s June onwards, after you have updated it twice or your 1-month period is over.

topics.title: Filing and Viewing Form GST PMT-09 for for transfer of amount (within same GSTIN) and for transfer of amount (to different GSTIN on same PAN)

items.q: What is Form GST PMT-09 and why is it used?

spans.s:
Form GST PMT-09 has been provided to registered taxpayers to transfer the amount from one Major Head & Minor Head (Tax, Interest, Penalty, Fee and Others) to another major & Minor Head for the same GSTIN(Integrated tax, Central tax, State/UT tax, and Cess) or from one GSTIN to another GSTIN obtained on same PAN (Integrated tax and Central tax only), in case he/she has wrongly deposited any amount in their cash ledger, by choosing the appropriate option made available on the portal as below:
 1. File GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (within same GSTIN)
 2. File GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (to different GSTIN on same PAN)

items.q: From where can I file Form GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (within same GSTIN) and for transfer of amount (to different GSTIN on same PAN)?

spans.s: To file GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (within same GSTIN), navigate to
Services > Ledgers > Electronic Cash Ledger > File GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (within same GSTIN)
To file GST PMT-09 for Transfer of amount (to different GSTIN on same PAN), navigate to
Services > Ledgers > Electronic Cash Ledger > File GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (to different GSTIN on same PAN).

items.q: Can I select more than one Minor Head under one Major Head while filing Form GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (within same GSTIN) and transfer of amount (to different GSTIN on same PAN)?

spans.s: Yes, you can select more than one Minor Heads while transferring amount from one head to another, one at a time, while filing Form GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (within same GSTIN) and transfer of amount (to different GSTIN on same PAN).

items.q: How can I add more than one Minor Head while filing Form GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (within same GSTIN) and transfer of amount (to different GSTIN on same PAN)?

spans.s: You can add more than one Minor Head for one selected Major Head using
Add Record
option before clicking
PROCEED TO FILE

items.q: Can I preview Form GST PMT-09 for both categories before filing?
items.section: Previewing and Signing Form GST PMT-09

spans.s: Yes, you can view/download Form GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (within same GSTIN) and transfer of amount (to different GSTIN on same PAN) in PDF format before filing the same on the GST Portal.

items.q: What are the modes of signing Form GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (within same GSTIN) and transfer of amount (to different GSTIN on same PAN)?
items.section: Previewing and Signing Form GST PMT-09

spans.s: You can file Form GST PMT-09 using DSC or EVC.

items.q: What will happen once Form GST PMT-09 is filed?
items.section: Post Filing of Form GST PMT-09

spans.s:
After Form GST PMT-09 is filed for either transfer of amount (within same GSTIN) or transfer of amount (to different GSTIN on same PAN) :
 • An ARN is generated on successful filing of Form GST PMT-09.
 • An SMS and an email is sent to the taxpayer on his registered mobile and email id.
 • Electronic Cash ledger gets updated after successful filing of Form GST PMT-09.
 • Filed form GST PMT-09 becomes available for view/download in PDF format.

items.q: Will I get any intimation once I file Form GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (within same GSTIN) and transfer of amount (to different GSTIN on same PAN)?

spans.s: Yes, you will receive SMS and e-mail on your registered e-mail ID and Mobile number, once Form GST PMT-09 is filed for both categories.

items.q: From where can I view filed Form GST PMT-09?

spans.s: To view filed Form GST PMT-09 for either category, navigate to
Services > Ledgers > Electronic Cash Ledger > View Filed GST PMT-09
option using Search By ARN or Search By Date.

items.q: From where can I download filed Form GST PMT-09?

spans.s: To download filed Form GST PMT-09 for either category, navigate to
Services > Ledgers > Electronic Cash Ledger > View Filed GST PMT-09 > Search by ARN or Date > ARN Hyperlink > DOWNLOAD GST PMT-09(PDF)
option.

items.q: Can I transfer amount between same Major Heads like from IGST (tax) to IGST (tax) while filing Form PMT-09?

spans.s: Yes, for
Form GST PMT-09 (transfer of amount to different GSTIN on same PAN)
, you can transfer from IGST (Tax) to IGST (Tax) of another GSTIN registered on the same PAN. Both the
Major Heads
and
Minor Heads

can be same for different GSTINs.
 However, for
Form GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount (within same GSTIN),

you cannot transfer the amount between the same major and Minor Head. For example, you cannot transfer from IGST (Tax) to IGST (Tax), but you can transfer from IGST (Tax) to any other major & Minor Head combination.
Reference Table is attached below:

header.s: Transfer between Major Heads(IGST, CGST, SGST and Cess)
Form GST PMT-09 (transfer of amount to different GSTIN on same PAN) Minor Heads (Tax, Interest, Penalty, Fee and Others)
Form GST PMT-09 for transfer of amount within same GSTIN Minor Heads (Tax, Interest, Penalty, Fee and Others)

rows.s: Allowed between all Minor Heads except for the same Minor Head
Allowed between all Minor Heads except for the same Minor Head
Allowed between all Minor Heads except for the same Minor Heads
Allowed between all Minor Heads except for the same Minor Heads

spans.s: Note
: Transfer of amount through Form GST PMT-09
(to different GSTIN registered on same PAN)
is only permissible for two Major Heads i.e. IGST and CGST.

items.q: After selecting the transferee GSTIN from the drop-down list, I am getting an error message. Why?

spans.s:
If there is only one GSTIN registered under transferor PAN, an error message will be displayed stating that,
 “There is no other GSTIN registered on this PAN.”

items.q: While entering the details in transfer amount from and transfer amount to, I am getting an error message. Why?

spans.s: If there is an un-stayed demand with positive value (Sum of values across all minor and Major Heads), the system will display the error:
“This facility is not available to taxpayer against whom liability is outstanding.”

topics.title: Negative Liability Statement

items.q: What is a Negative Liability Statement?

spans.s: In case there is any negative liability in a tax period and no amount is payable during that tax period by the taxpayer, then such negative liability is maintained by the GST Portal in Negative Liability Statement. The Balance, if any, lying in the Negative Liability Statement, will automatically be adjusted against the liability of subsequent tax period(s). The Negative Liability Statement is only for view purpose by the taxpayers and cannot be edited.

For Example: Composition taxpayers reports the liability as net of credit/debit notes. In some cases, value of credit notes exceeds the value of outward supplies. In such cases, the liability becomes negative. In such rare scenarios, where the taxpayers have negative liability in Form GST CMP-08 or Form GSTR-4 (Annual), the same is posted to Negative Liability Statement.
For E.g
.: If
Tax Amount of Outward Supplies (CGST+SGST)
Tax Amount of credit notes (CGST+SGST) issued
negative liability

rows.s: Tax component on Outward supplies during a tax period say Q1
Tax component of credit notes issued during the tax period Q1
Negative Liability (available for utilization towards supplies in future tax periods)
Tax component on Outward supplies made during next tax period say Q2
Tax amount adjusted against the Negative Liability
Negative Liability (available for utilization in future tax periods) say Q3

spans.s:
In above example, Rs 40000 will be posted as a credit entry in the Negative Liability Statement.
 In the next tax period if the total liability is Rs 30,000, then out of Rs 40,000, Rs 30,000 will be utilized. Then, there will be a debit entry posted in the Negative Liability Statement for Rs 30,000 and so on & so on.

items.q: Who are the taxpayers for whom the Negative Liability Statement is maintained?

spans.s: The Negative Liability Statement is maintained for taxpayers registered under composition levy as of now.

items.q: Where can the taxpayers view and download their Negative Liability Statement?
items.section: Viewing and Downloading Negative Liability Statement

spans.s: The Negative Liability Statement can be viewed for a maximum of 12 months at a time in the post-login mode by navigating
Services
Ledgers
Negative Liability Statement

.
 Negative Liability Statement can be downloaded in CSV format using the DOWNLOAD AS CSV button available on the bottom of the page.

items.q: What is the meaning of Debit/Credit as displayed in Negative Liability Statement?
items.section: Viewing and Downloading Negative Liability Statement

spans.s: The meaning of Debit is that the amount is debited or utilised and meaning of Credit is that the amount is credited or posted.

items.q: Is the Negative Liability Statement maintained separately for reverse charge and other than reverse charge liability?
items.section: Viewing and Downloading Negative Liability Statement

spans.s: Yes, the Negative Liability Statement is maintained for both reverse charge and other than reverse charge liability separately via different columns for each.

items.q: Can a GST Practitioner view my Negative Liability Statement?
items.section: Viewing and Downloading Negative Liability Statement

spans.s: Yes, a GST Practitioner can view your Negative Liability Statement who has been authorized by you.

items.q: As a taxpayer, I had some negative liability which was posted to Electronic liability register part -1. What will happen to such balances?

spans.s:
In case there is some negative liability amount which is posted to Electronic Liability Register part-1, the same will be transferred to the Negative Liability Statement. 
 Note: With the introduction of Negative Liability Statement, all the entries related to negative liability as well as adjustment of negative liability towards liability of succeeding tax periods is made through the Negative Liability Statement and not from the Electronic liability register part-I.

items.q: I have negative liability arising out of one type of Statement / Return. Can such negative liability be adjusted towards payment of liability of some other Statement / Return?

spans.s:
The negative liability arising from one Statement / Return can be adjusted against the liability of other Statement / Return.
 For example: You have some negative liability from Form CMP-08, the same can be adjusted while you are filing form GSTR-4, if there are any liabilities to be paid.

items.q: Can I adjust the negative liability arising from return for the payment of non-return liabilities?

spans.s: No, the negative liability, if any, arising from returns (Form GST CMP-08 or Form GSTR-4 Annual) cannot be adjusted for the payment of non-return related liability.

items.q: I have some balances in Negative Liability Statement. Can I make payments without using the same?

spans.s: No, you cannot make any payments related to returns (Form GST CMP-08 or Form GSTR-4 Annual) without using the balance as available in Negative Liability Statement.

items.q: Can negative liability arising under one head can be adjusted towards some other head?

spans.s: No, negative liability arising under one major head cannot be adjusted towards some other major head.

topics.title: Utilizing Cash/ ITC for Payment of Demand

items.q: What is utilization of cash/ ITC for payment of demand or any other amount due about?

spans.s: Utilization of cash/ ITC for payment of demand is about payments of non-return related liabilities. These liabilities are created through generation of Demand ID by tax officials, which is a reference number of the order or application, appearing in the Electronic Liability Register (Part-II).

items.q: From which ledger payments against the liabilities of a particular demand ID be made?

spans.s: The payments against the liabilities of a particular demand ID can be made by using the following ledgers:
• Cash balance available in the Electronic Cash Ledger; and/or
• Input tax credit balance available in the Electronic Credit Ledger.

items.q: How does the taxpayer get to know about outstanding demands?

spans.s: The taxpayer can get the information regarding outstanding demands from Electronic Liability Register (Part-II). This is shown in a table after logging in and navigating to Services > Ledgers > Electronic Liability Register > Part - II: Other than return related liabilities link

items.q: Who can access the functionality of “Utilize cash/ ITC for payment of demand or any other amount due”?

spans.s: The following persons can have access for the functionality of Utilizing cash/ITC for payment of demand or any other amount due:
• Registered taxpayer having a valid GSTIN or
• Person having temporary id or
• Taxpayers after cancellation of registration or
• Authorized/ Jurisdictional tax official

items.q: What are the pre-conditions for utilization of cash /ITC for payment of demand or any other amount due?

spans.s: The pre-conditions for utilization of cash /ITC for payment of demand or any other amount due are:
• Demand ID is already generated against which payment is yet to be made.
• User should have valid User ID and password and has necessary access for the same.

items.q: What are the details displayed to the taxpayer after selecting a Demand ID?

spans.s: The following details are displayed after user selects a Demand ID:-
• Outstanding liability towards tax, interest, penalty, fees and Others for IGST/CGST/SGST/UTGST/Cess against the selected Demand ID
• Balance as per Electronic Cash ledger
• Balance as per Electronic Credit Ledger

items.q: What are the details to be entered by the taxpayer after selecting a Demand ID for payment?

spans.s: The following details are to be entered by the taxpayer after selecting a Demand ID for payment:
• Amount intended to be paid
• Amount intended to be paid through Cash
• Amount intended to be paid through ITC

items.q: How is the relief towards reduced penalty available to the taxpayer, if payment is made within the specified period as per law?

spans.s: In case Demand ID is created under section 74 of the CGST/SGST/IGST/Cess Act, then as per law, GST Portal shows reduced payment liability towards penalty, if taxpayer makes payment, as per following conditions:

The penalty amount displayed is 50% of the amount stated in the order and the balance 50% of the penalty is waived off. A credit entry is passed in the Electronic Liability Register – Part II accordingly.

items.q: Can a user make part payment or multiple payments against a particular Demand ID?

spans.s: Yes, GST Portal allows user for making part payment at multiple occasions, against a particular demand ID, till the outstanding balance becomes zero.

items.q: Are there any conditions for a taxpayer to be eligible for waiver of penalty against a Demand ID?

spans.s: Only if the payment is made against a Demand ID, created under Section 74 of the Act, within the specified period of 30 days from the date of communication of the order, the taxpayer is eligible for waiver of 50% of the penalty levied in the order.
Following conditions must also be fulfilled:
• The amount of penalty waiver will be considered if the demands included in the order, is paid off completely, across the Acts.
• If the taxpayer doesn’t pay off the reduced penalty along with tax and interest in full, within 30 days, no entries of reduced penalty will be posted in the Liability Register – Part II.
• Non-payment of any amount included in the demand towards “others” or Fees” won’t be considered towards eligibility of waiver of 50% of the penalty amount.
• This convention will hold for each demand created under the aforesaid section.
• Such entry of waiver of penalty will be tagged against the same demand only for which the payment is being made.

items.q: How would the taxpayer know that the utilization of cash/ITC has been successful?

spans.s: On click of “Set-Off” button, if payment is successful, a success message is displayed along with PRN (Payment Reference Number) and all the relevant ledgers get updated.

items.q: What is Payment Reference Number?

spans.s: Payment Reference Number is a unique reference number for any payment transaction done on the GST Portal which gets posted to Electronic Liability Register Part-II.

items.q: Which ledgers of the taxpayer gets updated on utilization of cash/ITC?

spans.s: i. On utilization of ITC, Debit entry number is generated and posting is done against that demand ID in Electronic Liability Register Part-II as well as in the Electronic Credit Ledger.
ii. On utilization of Cash, Debit entry number is generated and posting is done against that demand ID in Electronic Liability Register Part-II as well as in the Electronic Cash Ledger.

iii. In case of full payment is made under Demand order raised under Section 74 of CGST/SGST Act read with section 20 of IGST Act or Section 21 of UTGST Act, an entry would be posted in the Electronic Liability Register - Part II for the 50% penalty waiver.

items.q: How does the taxpayer get to know about withdrawal entry made by the tax officer?

spans.s: Taxpayer will be able to view the withdrawal entry on the Case Details page. Remarks added by the tax officer while withdrawing FORM GST DRC-01D will not be appear. Also, an intimation will be sent to taxpayer immediately after withdrawal of Form GST DRC-01 through E-mail and SMS.

items.q: Where can Taxpayer make payment for the demand intimated through Form GST DRC-01D?

spans.s: Taxpayer will be able to make payment for the demand by navigating to
Services > Ledgers > Payment towards Demand

. Then, the taxpayer will be able to identify the demand ID created through intimation issued. Taxpayer will be able to make full as well as partial payment against such demand. Payment cannot be made more than the demand amount. Both Electronic Cash ledger and/or Electronic Credit ledger can be utilized for such payment.

topics.title: Export of Electricity without Payment of Tax (accumulated ITC)

items.q: How can I get my refund of Export of Electricity without Payment of Tax (accumulated ITC)?

spans.s: 1. You have to file the refund application in Form GST RFD 01 on the GST Portal under the category Export of Electricity without Payment of Tax (accumulated ITC) for the relevant tax period.

2. You have to provide the Turnover of Export of Electricity and the Adjusted Total Turnover for the period for which refund is claimed in Statement 3A, based on the electricity exported during that period.

3. The Net ITC in the table “Computation of Refund to be claimed” is auto-populated by the system and can be edited downwards considering net ITC availed for the heads of CGST/SGST/IGST together and Cess, in the return for the respective tax period for which refund is claimed, excluding any ITC related to Capital Goods, transition ITC that may have been posted in the ledger on account of transition ITC claims in the said period.
4. The system will auto calculate the Maximum Refund Amount in Statement 3A after you enter the turnover values and Net ITC, and this figure will appear in the last column of the computation table.

5. You must be careful while filling details in Form GST RFD 01 because no rectification is allowed after filing. You must ensure that:
 o All applicable returns, including GSTR 3B, for the refund period are filed,
 o You have exported electricity and have correctly prepared Statement 3B (offline utility) containing document details, REA details, generating station details, tariff per unit, energy exported, and scheduled energy,
 o The JSON file for Statement 3B is validated successfully on the GST Portal without any document errors.

6. Once the ARN is generated after filing the refund application, it will be assigned to the Jurisdictional Refund Processing Officer for review and processing. You may track the refund status using the Track Application Status option on the portal.

items.q: What are the relied upon documents which I have to upload with refund application for ITC refund?

spans.s:
You must upload all documents required to be filed along with Form RFD‑01, as prescribed under the CGST Rules, relevant Circulars, and any additional documents requested by the refund‑sanctioning authority.
 In addition, the following documents are mandatory:
 • Filling Statement 3B
 • Annexure I – PDF format, maximum size 5 MB
 • Agreement detailing the tariff per unit – PDF format, maximum size 10 MB

items.q: Can I file nil refund for multiple tax period in one refund application?

spans.s: Yes, NIL refund can be filed for multiple tax periods in one application.

items.q: From where can I download the utility to upload the statement?

spans.s: Navigate to Services > Refunds > Application for Refund > Select the refund type > Download Offline Utility link.

items.q: What is the purpose of Download Offline Utility to upload the statement?

spans.s: Download Offline Utility is provided to enter and upload details in Statement 3B of documents against which refund is being claimed.

items.q: What happens when refund application is filed?

spans.s:
• GST Portal generates an ARN and displays it in a confirmation message, indicating that the refund application has been successfully filed.
 • GST Portal sends the ARN to registered e-mail ID and mobile number of the registered taxpayer.
 • GST Portal also makes a Debit entry in the Electronic Credit Ledger for the amount claimed as refund.

items.q: What is ARN?

spans.s: Once the refund application is filed, an Application Reference Number (ARN) will be generated. The ARN will also be sent to your registered email address and mobile number. This ARN can additionally be used to track the status of your refund application.

items.q: Can I preview the refund application before filing?

spans.s: Yes, you can preview the refund application in PDF format to check for any inconsistency or discrepancy before filing on the GST Portal.

items.q: How can I track the status of application for refund?

spans.s: To track your filed application, navigate to
Services > Refunds > Track Application Status
option.

items.q: Where can I download my filed refund application?

spans.s: Navigate to
Services > User Services > My Applications
link to download your refund application.

items.q: Can I view the details of refund claimed in Electronic Credit Ledger?

spans.s: Yes, you can view the debit entry in the Electronic Credit Ledger for the amount claimed as refund.

items.q: What are the relied upon documents which I have to upload with refund application for ITC refund?

spans.s: You have to upload documents as are required to be filed along with Form RFD-01 as notified under CGST Rules or Circulars issued in the matter and other such documents the refund sanctioning authority may require.

items.q: To whom should I file my application with?

spans.s: The taxpayer shall file the refund application in Form RFD-01 on GST portal. After filing, refund application shall be assigned to Refund Processing Officer and refund applicant can track the status of refund application.

items.q: Can I file for multiple tax periods from two different financial years in one refund application?

spans.s: Yes, you can file for multiple tax periods from two different financial years in one refund application.

items.q: Can nil period of refund be combined with the period in which there is refund in one application?

spans.s:
Yes, a nil‑refund period can be combined with periods in which refund is applicable and filed together in a single refund application.
 For example, if you want to file a refund for the period April–September, and the months of May–June are nil‑refund months, you have two options:
 1. File separate applications:
 • File a normal refund application for April.
 • File a Nil Refund application for May–June.
 • File another normal refund application for July–September.
 2. File a single consolidated application:
 Select the tax period April–September and file one normal refund application covering the entire period, including the nil months.

items.q: What is the purpose of Download Offline Utility to upload the statement?

spans.s: Download Offline Utility is provided to enter and upload details in Statement 3B of documents against which refund is being claimed.

items.q: Whether I would be able to file refund application without uploading statement of documents?

spans.s: No. Statement of documents is mandatory for filing refund application.

The statement uploaded by taxpayer would be validated with the data already declared by the taxpayer while filing return. Only after this data is validated, the taxpayer would be able to file the refund application.

items.q: What is the significance of VALIDATE STATEMENT button?

spans.s: The Validate Statement button is used to verify the document details uploaded by the taxpayer against the data declared in Form GSTR‑1/GSTR‑1A.

items.q: Can I change data after clicking the VALIDATE STATEMENT button?

spans.s: Yes, you can change data even after you have validated the uploaded statement. If you want to update/delete the statement, then you would have to first delete the whole statement by clicking the
DELETE STATEMENT
button and upload a new statement of documents again if needed.

items.q: What is the purpose of Download Unique Documents?

spans.s: The purpose of Download unique Documents is to see the successfully uploaded documents on the GST Portal by clicking on the hyperlink Download Unique Documents.

items.q: What is the purpose of Download Invalid Documents?

spans.s: The purpose of Download Invalid Documents is to see the documents that have not been uploaded successfully along with error details on the GST Portal by clicking on the hyperlink Download Invalid Documents.

items.q: I am getting a message "validated with error" while uploading statement on the GST Portal. What do I do?

spans.s: In case any statement is validated with error, click the Download Invalid Document link. Open the invalid document excel sheet. Error details are displayed. You can only rectify the error details in the JSON file and upload on the GST Portal again by clicking the CLICK HERE TO UPLOAD button.

items.q: I have uploaded statement which has been validated on the GST Portal. I need to upload a new statement of documents again. What do I do?

spans.s: If you don't have any error and statement has been validated, and then you want to update/delete the statement, then you would have to first delete the whole statement by clicking the DELETE STATEMENT button and upload a new statement of documents again if needed.

items.q: In which bank account will the refund amount be credited? Is it one of the accounts that I registered in GST Portal?

spans.s: Yes, the refund amount will be credited to one of the bank accounts that you have added while filing your registration application on the GST Portal. At the time of filling out form RFD-01, you will be required to select a bank account from the list of your linked / registered accounts in the GST Portal for crediting refund to that account, from the dropdown available in refund application. In case you want refund in another preferred bank account which is not appearing in the drop down list, you will have to add that bank account by filing amendment of registered (non-core) form. The bank account added by amendment form will get added to the drop-down list.

items.q: What will be the impact of GSTR-1A , on refund applications filed by the taxpayer?

spans.s: As of now the validations in the refund applications are done from the taxpayer or supplier’s GSTR-1 and the validation will check whether the details entered in the specific categories of refund utility are matching with the taxpayer's and supplier’s GSTR-1. With the introduction of new form GSTR-1A, the validations will be done from both GSTR-1 and GSTR-1A.

items.q: What should I do if my refund application is rejected for re-credit of rejected amount ?

spans.s: If your GST refund application is rejected (fully or partially), you can request that the rejected amount be re-credited to your Electronic Credit Ledger (for ITC-based refunds) or Electronic Cash Ledger (for cash refunds). To enable this, you must file an undertaking on the GST portal confirming that you will not appeal against the rejected amount. Based on this undertaking, the proper officer will issue an order in Form GST PMT-03 to process the re-credit.

items.q: When / how will the refund Form RFD-01 be processed?

spans.s:
Once the refund application in Form RFD‑01 is filed and the ARN is generated, the application along with all supporting documents is automatically assigned to the Jurisdictional Authority for further examination and processing.
 The taxpayer can also track the status of the refund application anytime using the Track Status functionality on the portal.

topics.title: Refund of tax paid on Inward Supplies of goods by Canteen Store Department (CSD) (Form GST RFD-10A)

spans.s:
Login to GST portal for filing refund application

items.q: What is chronological/sequential filing?

spans.s: Chronological or sequential filing refers to the process of filing each refund application in a sequential order for every quarter, regardless of whether there is a refund amount to claim or not.
For Example:

A CSD wants to file two refunds for the periods Jan 2024 to March 2024 and July 2024 to September 2024. In GST system, the CSD has to file the first refund by selecting the period Jan 2024 to March 2024. When the CSD tries to file the second refund claim for the period July 2024 to September 2024, the GST portal will prompt the user to file refund for the period April 2024 – June 2024.If there is no refund claim for the period April 2024 – June 2024, then NIL refund claim has to be filed for the said period. Post that, the GST portal will allow the CSD to file refund for the period July 2024 to September 2024.

items.q: Why is NIL filing required?

spans.s: If there is no refund amount for a particular quarter, or if a taxpayer has already filed manual claims for the earlier periods, a NIL refund application should be filed for that quarter to maintain the Chronological order of filing. This ensures smooth filing of refund application for the subsequent quarters.
Example:

A CSD wants to file a refund claim (RFD 10A) for the period April – June 2024 in GST system and all their earlier CSD refund claims are filed manually till the period March 2024. The said CSD has to file NIL refund claims in the GST system for the period from June 2017 – March 2024 in the GST portal though manual refund claims are filed for the said period. This will enable the taxpayer to file CSD refund claim for the period April – June 2024.

items.q: Can I file for multiple tax periods from two different financial years in one refund application?

spans.s: Yes, you can file refund for multiple tax periods from two different financial years in one refund application.
For Example:

a. You can file separate refund applications in Form GST RFD- 10A for the quarter ending March 2020 and quarter ending June 2020.
 b. You can club these two quarters in a single refund application in Form GST RFD- 10A for the quarter ending March 2020 and quarter ending June 2020.

items.q: Can I file nil refund for multiple tax period in one refund application?

spans.s: Yes, you can file for nil refund for multiple tax period in one refund application.

items.q: Can I enter Bank Account details manually while applying for refund of CSD?

items.q: Can I file CSD Refund application on monthly basis.

topics.title: Refund on Account of "Any other" ground of reason

items.q: When the refund application on account of “Any Other” ground of reason can be filed?

spans.s: Refund application on account of “Any Other” ground of reason can be filed, when the taxpayer wants to claim refund for any reason, for which there is no specific refund application available in the refunds section. Therefore, if there is no option to claim refund for the specific reason for which refund is claimed, then taxpayer needs to click on “Any Other” ground of reason and specify his reason in the refund application while filing refund.
Note:

Taxpayer should have filed the applicable return (GSTR-1/ GSTR3B/ CPM-08/ GSTR-4 (Annual)) which were due to be furnished on or before the date on which the refund application is filed and taxpayer must have filed the latest GSTR-3B for the period for which refund has been filed or for the invoices for which refund has been claimed.

items.q: What are the relied upon documents which I have to upload with refund application?

spans.s: You have to upload documents as are required to be filed along with Form RFD-01, as notified under CGST Rules or Circulars issued in the matter and other such documents the refund sanctioning authority may require.

A certificate in Annexure 2 issued by a chartered accountant or a cost accountant to the effect that the incidence of tax, interest or any other amount claimed as refund has not been passed on to any other person, in a case where the amount of refund claimed exceeds two lakh rupees is to be provided. Therefore, if the refund amount claimed is more than 2 lacs, then taxpayer needs to mandatorily upload Certificate in Annexure 2.
Taxpayers have an option to upload 10 documents with the refund application, of size up to 5 MB each.

items.q: When refund application on account of excess payment of tax can be filed?

spans.s: Refund application on account of excess payment of tax can be filed, when the taxpayer has paid excess tax (in the form of advance tax or tax deducted/collected at source or self-assessment tax or payment of tax on regular assessment) against the tax required to be paid by him.

items.q: Who all can file refund application using ground as “Excess payment of Tax”?

spans.s: Normal and casual taxpayers filing Form GSTR-3B, composite taxpayers filing Form GSTR-4 and Non-Resident taxpayers filing Form GSTR-5 can file refund application using ground as “Excess payment of Tax.”

items.q: What is the minimum amount that can be claimed while filing refund application using ground as “Excess payment of Tax”?

spans.s: Refund can be claimed for the amount of Rs.1000 or more while filing refund application using ground as “Excess payment of Tax”.

In case, the refund amount claimed is more than 2 lacs, then the taxpayer needs to mandatorily upload Certificate from CA/ICWA in Annexure 2 to the refund application. In case, refund claimed amount is less than 2 lacs, then the certificate is not required, taxpayer needs to provide self-declaration only.

spans.s: The following conditions must be met, for being eligible to file Form RFD-01, to claim refund on account of Export of Services (with payment of tax):

items.s: The taxpayer is registered with GST Portal and holds an active GSTIN during the period for which refund is being applied for.

Taxpayer has paid taxes on the services exported, for which tax payer wants to claim refund.
Tax payer have BRC/FIRC number details for the export document, which is to be mentioned while claiming refund.
Any other criteria as prescribed.

Tax periods commencing from 01.04.2018, registered persons will be allowed to file the refund application in Form GST RFD-01 on the GST Portal subject to the condition that the amount of refund of integrated tax/cess claimed should not be more than the amount of integrated tax/cess mentioned in the table under column 3.1(b) of Form GSTR-3B filed for the corresponding tax period.
